CORRECTED RE-SCORE + STACK PUSHED — S6's in-scope evidence is complete.

## The corrected verdict, offline re-score of the already-recorded run (zero model calls)

                        BEFORE (broken metric)                          AFTER (62ac fixed)
  standard   1 decision flip                                    1 decision flip  (unchanged)
  frontier   agreement 0.929 | 2 flips | FALSE-ACCEPT ROSE 0.143  agreement 0.929 | 2 flips

THE FRONTIER FALSE-ACCEPT FAILURE IS GONE, and the corrected numbers invert its meaning:
  frontier false_accept   v1 0.214  vs  v2 0.071
Bedrock false-fires LESS THAN A THIRD as often as direct Anthropic, and the old predicate was failing
the run FOR THAT IMPROVEMENT. That was the whole of 62ac.

635f's fix changed NOTHING on this data, exactly as predicted before it ran — error rate was 0.000 on
all four arms and every flipped pair is errored=False/valid=True, so there were no errored pairs to
exclude. The prediction holding is itself a check that the fix is correctly scoped.

RAW MEASUREMENT INTEGRITY VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: the `records` arrays are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the
original recording (72f863b5a2) and the re-scored artifact (30 -> 30 both slots, no keys added or
removed). Only `gating_failures` and `metrics` moved — the derived fields. The measurement was not
re-run and was not altered.

WHAT REMAINS FAILING IS OUT OF SCOPE BY OPERATOR RULING: verdict agreement 0.929 and the decision
flips compare two DIFFERENT MODELS' judgements. Non-determinism between models is expected and is not
an S6 failure. These are recorded as informational, per the retargeted ACs.

## One artifact regression, flagged rather than left to be discovered

`metrics.latency_s` went from real measurements to 0.0 on both slots:
  standard  v1 2756.5 / v2 2484.6  ->  0.0 / 0.0
  frontier  v1 2103.1 / v2 2105.1  ->  0.0 / 0.0
The re-score recomputes from `records`, which carry no latency, so the informational latency is
zeroed rather than preserved. NOT LOST — the real numbers survive in git at 72f863b5a2 and in this
ticket's earlier ParityReport comment — but the current artifact understates them, and the ACs ask for
the informational per-arm latency. Worth either preserving latency across a re-score or stating in the
artifact that 0.0 means "not recomputed" rather than "instantaneous".

## Stack pushed to Gerrit

  1266  0d76: add the Bedrock provider-parity harness
  1267  0d76: run corpus items concurrently
  1268  0d76: record the live Bedrock parity run
  1269  62ac: fix the inverted parity false-accept metric
  1270  635f: exclude errored pairs from parity flips
  1271  0d76: prove payload and tool parity      <- stack tip

Three tickets share the branch because 62ac/635f were deliberately worked in this worktree (it holds
the recorded results they needed to re-score). Every commit carries an in-epic `rebar-ticket:` trailer;
the interleaving is intentional and the ordering is coherent.

## In-scope S6 evidence, now complete

  PAYLOAD PARITY  system/messages/tools byte-identical across providers; the MODEL ID is the only
                  differing field. Captured at the provider boundary with zero network calls.
  TOOL PARITY     6 tools, identical names/descriptions/input schemas, both providers, both slots.
  CAPABILITY      one difference, and it is MODEL-driven not PROVIDER-driven: temperature=0.0 is sent
                  to sonnet on BOTH providers and withdrawn from opus on BOTH. Mutation-proven — the
                  symmetry test goes RED if the supports_temperature override is deleted.
  ENVELOPE        8 differences enumerated. Seven are spelling. ONE IS SUBSTANTIVE: Bedrock's
                  `cachePoint` carries NO TTL where Anthropic's `cache_control` carries ttl="5m".
                  Latent today (rebar sets no non-default TTL) but a real expressiveness gap — flag to S8.
  PROVIDER-CLEAN  zero non-Bedrock calls on 84/84 v2 case-runs, both slots (recorded earlier).
